Information since June points to continued labor-market strength and real activity growing at a strong pace, with inflation and longer-run expectations near 2 percent—consistent with gradual, data-dependent rate normalization and “balanced risks.” Incorporating the April 2018 SLOOS, however, the credit channel shows mixed signals: banks reported widened loan rate spreads, changes in commercial real estate credit policies and demand, and largely unchanged standards for qualified jumbo mortgages. These survey insights suggest lending conditions are not uniformly easing and add a mild headwind to an otherwise solid macro backdrop. Netting these, the tone remains positive but slightly tempered by tighter pricing and CRE cross-currents.
